To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the wet oxidation method is not suitable for the preparation of plant tissue samples for LSC and that the Van Slyke wet oxidation method and the Schoniger dry oxidation method are superior to the wet method of Mahin & Lofberg and to solubilization with Hyamine.
The Van Slyke wet oxidation method is the most accurate and reliable method for the preparation of samples for liquid sc intillation counting.

“The Van Slyke wet digestion method and the dry combustion in the Schoniger Micro-Mat BF5010 oxidation system are superior to the wet combustion of Mahin and the solubilization of plant tissue in Hyamine for the preparation of plant tissue samples for scintillation counting.”
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of a method for the determination of 14 C in plant tissue.
the development and application of new methods for the preparation and analysis of radioactive compounds, especially in the field of plant biochemistry and physiology.
the development of a rapid, accurate, reproducible method of preparing plant material for liquid scintillaton counting.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the Van Slyke wet oxidation and dry combustion methods should be used for routine analysis of plant material for 14 C, and the solubilization method for special cases, where the other methods are unsuitable.
, for routine purposes, Schoniger combustion in the Micro-mat BF 5011 is the method of choice, because it is the fastest, the simplest and most reliable.
Van Slyke wet oxidation and dry oxidation in the Schoniger combustion unit are the methods of choice for preparing plant tissue samples of up to 10 mg for liquid scintillography.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, if the amount of plant tissue available for analysis is small (e.g., less than 10 mg dry wt.), Schoniger dry oxidation in the Micro-Met BF 5010 system is the method of choice.
Van Slyke wet oxidation is the most reliable method of preparation of 14C-labelled plant tissue samples for scintillation counting, while Schoniger dry oxidation is the most rapid and simple method.
Van Slyke wet oxidation and Schoniger dry oxidation are the methods of choice for routine work in our laboratory.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Van Slyke and Schoniger combustion methods are superior for the determination of radioactivity in plant tissues.
the Schoniger dry oxidation method is superior to the wet combustion method for the preparation of small samples of 14 C-labeled plant material for liquid scintillography.
Van Slyke wet oxidation and Schoniger dry oxidation methods are superior to wet oxidation method of Mahin and Lofber and Hyamine method.
